description: The gprMax development team publishes an open-source finite-difference time-domain solver for electromagnetic wave propagation, originally developed for ground-penetrating radar. Zenodo archives version 3.1.5 from April 2019, with source and documentation in the linked repository. Its versioned README and licence specify GPL version 3 or later and free access. The Python/Cython implementation solves three-dimensional Maxwell equations with an OpenMP CPU solver and optional NVIDIA CUDA acceleration. Configurable geometry, materials, sources and receiver outputs support simulation of subsurface inspection, antennas and interactions with built infrastructure. No related catalogue or first-review draft explicitly covers this platform. Spatial and temporal resolution depend on model inputs; infrastructure applications require appropriate geometry and material calibration. The current repository describes a substantially newer version 4, whose additional features must not be attributed to this archived release. Build compatibility, numerical convergence and model uncertainty were not independently tested; software was not installed.
